quotes.text: A temperature reading, a fault code, or a machine stop does not create value just because it entered a cloud platform. It creates value when it changes a named decision in time for that decision to matter.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes the value of industrial telemetry around decisions rather than data volume.

quotes.text: If those names don't resolve to a single approved asset identity, any AI system will get four partial stories about one physical machine. That's not an AI problem, it's a data model problem
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows why shared asset identity must come before adding AI to factory data.

quotes.text: A generative AI model doesn't calculate a feasible plan just by describing those constraints well. A planning engine, a constraint solver, or defined business rules can test possible schedules against explicit limits.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Draws a clear line between generative AI explanation and deterministic production scheduling.

quotes.text: a notification only opens work, while a closed loop records what someone chose, sends that choice to the place where work happens, and captures the result so the next decision can improve.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines what closed loop really means beyond sending alerts.

quotes.text: A stream with visible data quality issues can improve. A stream that hides them slowly becomes fiction.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable argument for treating bad data as a visible operational condition.

takeaways: A machine event is a fact, not a decision: value only appears when it changes a named decision with a clear owner in time.
Shared asset identities, data contracts and context joins to MES, ERP and planning data must come before AI or automated escalation.
Use Fabric Real-Time Intelligence and Activator for awareness and tracked workflows, APS for feasible plans, and keep machine control local and safe.
hook: Many factories stream machine data to the cloud and build live dashboards, yet a stopped line still ends with someone calling the planner. This episode is for manufacturing, OT and data architects who want to connect a machine fault to a changed production decision. It walks through the full pipeline from edge and event transport through Fabric Real-Time Intelligence, context, APS and governed write-back.
